extra.message: User-supplied query parameter `username` (read from the request URL on line 8) is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string passed to `Jinja2.from_string()` and then rendered. This is a classic Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) sink: an attacker can supply a value such as `?username={{7*7}}` or `?username={{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}` to evaluate arbitrary expressions in the Jinja2 sandbox, potentially leading to remote code execution. The safe implementation in the comment (line 17) demonstrates the proper fix: pass the value via the render context rather than interpolating it into the template source.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
